section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the verse "And Avraham was old, advanced in days, and Hashem blessed Avraham with everything," and questions the meaning of "everything" as a hidden, boundless source.
section.t: "And Avraham was old, advanced in days, and Hashem blessed Avraham with everything."
And the Rebbe [the Rebbe Rashab]
(the Rebbe Shalom Ber)
of blessed memory, in his maamar beginning with this discourse
(from the year 5666),
precisely notes that it says "with everything" in a general way, and does not specify with what He blessed him.
And the point of the explanation:
"Everything" is the aspect of the essential concealment,
from which all revelations are drawn.
As it is brought in the Zohar
on the verse "And Hashem blessed Avraham with everything,"
that Avraham was blessed from the place from which all blessings emanate.
Therefore it says "with everything" in a general way and does not specify details,
because it is the aspect of the boundless, which is above details.
And one must understand the connection and relevance of the Zohar's interpretation that "everything" is the place from which all blessings emanate, with Rashi's commentary on the verse,
that "everything" refers to Yitzchak
("everything" in gematria equals "ben" [son]).
And also,
from the continuation of the verses it seems that this verse
("And Avraham was old, etc.")
is an introduction to "And Avraham said to his servant, etc., 'And you shall take a wife for my son, for Yitzchak.'"
And one must understand what is the connection of "And Hashem blessed Avraham with everything,"
that he was blessed from the place from which all blessings emanate,
to this—that he sent his servant to take a wife for his son.
Also, one must understand the greatness of the elevation of the marriage of Yitzchak and Rivkah, that it is loftier even than the aspect of "everything"
(the place from which all blessings emanate),
to the point that this—that Hashem blessed Avraham with everything—is only an introduction to the marriage of Yitzchak and Rivkah.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Avraham's ten trials correspond to the ten Sefiros, while "everything" refers to the innermost aspect of Kesser, which is beyond human arousal.
section.t: And this will be understood by prefacing what is brought in the Midrash:

"The Holy One, blessed be He, does not elevate a person to greatness until He tests and examines him, etc. And so you find with Avraham our father: the Holy One, blessed be He, tested him with ten trials, and he withstood them, and afterwards He blessed him, as it is said, 'And Hashem blessed Avraham with everything.'"
And the Tzemach Tzedek explains,
that the ten trials correspond to the ten Sefiros,
whereas "everything" is the innermost aspect of Kesser, which is not
included in the count of the ten Sefiros.
For in that aspect,
no arousal from below reaches there.
And after Avraham withstood the ten trials corresponding to the ten Sefiros, in which arousal from below is relevant,
then He blessed him with "everything,"
the innermost aspect of Kesser.
And it can be said,
that this is also the precise language of the verse: "And Avraham was old, advanced in days, and Hashem blessed Avraham with everything"—
that this—that he was old, advanced in days,
even though it is a blessing from the Holy One, blessed be He,
the verse attributes it to Avraham
("And Avraham was old, advanced in days"),
whereas regarding "everything," it does not say that Avraham had "everything," but rather that "Hashem blessed Avraham with everything."
The explanation of this can be said:
That which he was blessed with old age and days is an arousal from above that is aroused and drawn down by means of an arousal from below,
the service of Avraham,
whereas that which he was blessed with "everything" is an arousal from above that comes from above, to which no arousal from below reaches.
[And that this blessing came specifically after he withstood the ten trials is because there must be a place
that is complete],
therefore it is written regarding it, "And Hashem blessed, etc."
